reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Bio: Mario Garza is the artist and researcher behind Symbolic Studies, a project sharing symbolic insights on the zodiac, mythology, folklore and world religions, with astrology as its foundation. A lifelong artist who has worked as an art director and graphic designer for nearly 25 years, he runs Symbolic Studies from the Pacific Northwest alongside his wife Michelle, who co-hosts the podcast with him. His work traces syncretic threads across tarot, occultism and comparative religion, including the argument that the major deities of antiquity were originally polar gods before a solar model was laid over them. He also offers symbolic birth chart and tarot readings, private lessons and freelance design.
reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Name: Mario Garza

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Symbol or Living Guide", "body": "Chance opens with the question he wants held through the whole talk: is the psychopomp only symbolism pointing at nature, or a being that actually exists? If all is mind, he reasons, the first emanation from the divine source could be the trunk of the tree that all life branches from, and the guide met after death might be the oldest, eternal part of ourselves. Asked where he leans, Mario says he is inclined to think most everything is essentially a metaphor, likening the guide to a traveler returning from an exotic land, while leaving room to update his view."}, {"title": "Etruscan Faces of the Guide", "body": "Chance's slideshow leans on older Etruscan figures. He presents Vanth, a winged figure on funerary urns bearing a torch, key and scroll, often paired with Charun, whose hammer and the underworld krater he appears on lead Chance to suspect a link with Vulcan. Asked to read the images, Mario spots what looks like a noose hanging between Charun's legs. Chance then reads about Suri, a god of volcanoes and fire known to the Romans as Apollo Soranus, whose wolf priests on Mount Soracte reportedly walked barefoot over burning coals, and argues that the name Hades derives from an epithet of Suri."}, {"title": "Letter Swaps Beneath the Names", "body": "Chance applies philology throughout, cautioning that each added letter swap makes a link stretchier. Swapping V for B and T for D, he hears Vanth in the Buddhist bardo, and he returns to the swaps again and again. Chance says it blew his mind when he noticed that Pater, as in Dis Pater, might hide the ancient Greek word for a rudder, pedalion, which would make the father a steersman, though he calls it spitballing. He also links Orcus to Argus and to the ark that preserves life through catastrophe, and, reading Godfrey Higgins's Anacalypsis, suggests a thread worth exploring between the Etruscan Tinia and the Chinese Tian."}, {"title": "Libra's Scales and the Polar Axis", "body": "Speaking in Libra season, Mario finds it fitting that the seventh sign is the one that carries us into the underworld. He reads the scales through twin pillar symbolism, Boaz and Jachin, with a central pillar, the middle way, serving as the vertical axis that makes any scale work. Mario then shares an entry from Jean Chevalier's symbolic dictionary: at the equinoxes the pointer of the scales becomes the changeless polar axis, in ancient China the Great Bear was called the Jade Scales, and the Sanskrit word for scales, tula, also names the holy land at the pole. He ties this to the weighing of souls."}, {"title": "Twins, Placentas and the Shades", "body": "Twin symbolism keeps surfacing. Chance notes that Yama's name can mean twin and that Xolotl was the twin of Quetzalcoatl, the evening and morning phases of Venus. He argues that the closest twin and guardian each of us has is the placenta, which he believes carries its own spirit, and says Biofield Tuning sessions showed him how much birth stories shape people. Gabe, fighting phone troubles, sends a voice message calling Hades the Lord of the shades and counting seven gates. Chance also speculates, admittedly conjecturally, that ill intentioned souls may persuade the newly dead not to go into the light."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: In this Vibe Rant, Mario Garza (Symbolic Studies) and I explore the psychopomp archetype, the guide of deceased beings to and through the underworld. Do the symbolic links between Chthonic & underworld Gods across cultures and times point to a metaphysical reality to these shepherds of souls?
